question: Let $A$ and $B$ be independent events. Show that $A$ and $B'$ are also independent.
explanation:
Step 1: Independence relation
Since $A$ and $B$ are independent, $$P(A\cap B)=P(A)P(B).$$
Step 2: Decomposition of event $A$
The events $A\cap B$ and $A\cap B'$ are mutually exclusive and their union is $A$. Hence, $$P(A)=P(A\cap B)+P(A\cap B').$$
Step 3: Determination of $P(A\cap B')$
Therefore, $$P(A\cap B')=P(A)-P(A\cap B).$$ Using independence of $A$ and $B$, $$P(A\cap B')=P(A)-P(A)P(B).$$
Step 4: Factorisation
$$P(A\cap B')=P(A)[1-P(B)]=P(A)P(B').$$
Step 5: Conclusion
Since $$P(A\cap B')=P(A)P(B'),$$ the condition for independence is satisfied. Hence, $$\boxed{A\text{ and }B'\text{ are independent}.}$$

options.A: $A$ and $B'$ are independent because $P(A\cap B')=P(A)-P(A\cap B)=P(A)[1-P(B)]=P(A)P(B')$
options.B: $A$ and $B'$ are mutually exclusive because $B$ and $B'$ are mutually exclusive
